idiom_name: begin/rescue (or the rescue modifier) with retry, Hash#fetch for leaf defaults
implementation_notes: Ruby's rescue is the substitution mechanism and it is cheap to scope: the rescue modifier on a single expression, begin/rescue for a block, and method-body rescue for a whole call - with retry (valid only inside rescue) as the bounded recovery attempt. What replaces the classic degraded-mode object is the method's return value plus a small contract: Hash#fetch(key, default) and dig cover the leaf fallbacks, safe navigation (&.) avoids nil chains, and the degraded state travels in the returned value or a policy object. Keep the rescue class list narrow and record the degradation inside the rescue body.
code_sketch:
report = begin
           backend.report(id)
         rescue Timeout::Error, Backend::Unavailable => e
           Metrics.increment("degraded")
           logger.warn(e.message)
           Cache.fetch(id, ttl: 300) { Report.placeholder }
         end
render(report, degraded: report.degraded?)
pitfalls: A method-body rescue without a class list catches StandardError, including bugs inside the method itself; list the dependency's exception classes or wrap only the call.
retry inside rescue re-runs the body (and its side effects) forever unless attempts are bounded and backed off.
nil substitutes flow into views and presenters and produce the very errors the fallback was meant to avoid - return a Null Object or an explicit default.
